newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev loses 18 pct versus dlr in day.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev loses 18 pct versus dlr in day.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 590-605 per dollar on Friday, down from 575-585 in the morning and 507-510 at Monday's close as dollar demand topped supply in light interbank volume, dealers said.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was not seen selling dollars to halt the lev slide during the first trading day of 1997 for the local interbank market, dealers said.
BNB officials were not available for comment. Local markets were closed from Tuesday through Thursday for the New Year.
"The lev lost some 18 percent on the day because dollar demand coming mainly from small final clients heavily outweighed supply," a commercial bank dealer said. @

Trade was very thin in the afternoon because there were just a few foreign currency bidders left in the market while dollar supply rose slightly due to profit taking, helping the lev consolidate near 600 per dollar, another trader said.
"Dollar rates above 600 per dollar were deemed too high at the moment and many bidders withdrew from the market in the afternoon," the second dealer said.

BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that BNB powers to counter pressure on the lev through interventions were limited because payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt in 1997 would be a priority for the BNB.

Low BNB foreign exchange reserves, lack of financing from abroad and lower than expected privatisation proceeds in 1996 were the reasons why the central bank could not prevent a lev decline, Filipov said.
BNB forex reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November last year. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
